story.headline: LJ Martin's injury poses stiff challenge to No. 8 BYU's offense as Cougars host Iowa State
paragraphs: An injury to LJ Martin changes everything for No. 8 BYU on offense ahead of Friday’s clash with Iowa State.

Martin is expected to be sidelined for four to six weeks after suffering a lower-body injury against TCU. The senior running back had two carries for 16 yards in the Cougars’ 17-10 win over the Horned Frogs before exiting the game and not returning.

Martin’s absence is a significant blow to BYU’s offense. He was the Big 12’s leading rusher last season, tallying 1,305 yards and 12 touchdowns. The Cougars mustered just 216 total yards against the Horned Frogs in his absence.

With Martin unavailable, the Cougars will rely on multiple backs to shoulder the load in the backfield. Preston Rex and Journee Tonga should both see increased carries after filling in for Martin against TCU.

story.headline: No. 7 Indiana faces road test against Nebraska before showdown with Ohio State
paragraphs: With a huge home game on deck next week against Ohio State, Indiana coach Curt Cignetti hasn't had to get creative to find a way to keep his players locked in on the immediate task at hand. Not with a visit to Nebraska up next on Saturday.

“Well, it’s a Big Ten game on the road against an undefeated team so it’s a huge challenge, which we have to respond to, and our guys will be excited to play,” Cignetti said. “I’ve never been to Nebraska. I’ve never been to the state of Nebraska, and I’m looking forward to it. I’ve heard great things about the stadium, the fans. Obviously great tradition and history there through the years.”

No. 7 Indiana (5-0, 2-0 Big Ten) and Nebraska (5-0, 2-0) are two of the three Big Ten teams without a loss, and the defending national champion Hoosiers will carry a 21-game win streak into Memorial Stadium. The Hoosiers are 7.5-point favorites against a team that has lost 30 straight against Top 25 opponents.

The backdrop is similar to two years ago in Bloomington, Indiana. It was the Hoosiers' seventh game under Cignetti and, after winning their first six by a total of 196 points, Nebraska was billed as their toughest opponent to date. The Huskers turned over the ball five times in Indiana's 56-7 win.

story.headline: No. 1 Texas has reversed role and a reminder in Red River game against 2-loss unranked Oklahoma
paragraphs: Coach Steve Sarkisian and No. 1 Texas certainly know about going into their Red River rivalry game already with two losses, like Oklahoma has now, and what can happen next.

The Longhorns (4-0, 1-0 Southeastern Conference) were in that exact position last October. They had plummeted from preseason No. 1 to unranked for the game in the middle of the State Fair of Texas, then beat previously undefeated No. 6 Oklahoma.
“We were a desperate football team and found a way to win in the second half,” Sarkisian said this week. “So we know what it is.”

That is a bitter rivalry going into its 122nd game in the series that Texas leads 65-51-5. Fans in burnt orange and crimson are split at the 50-yard line inside the historic 92,100-seat Cotton Bowl Stadium, where the game will be played for the 90th year in a row on Saturday.

story.headline: No. 3 Notre Dame looks to extend school-record double-digit win margin streak when it hosts Stanford
paragraphs: No. 3 Notre Dame has emerged as a model of consistency in this ever-changing college football world.
The storied program has won 15 straight games, all by double digits, putting the Fighting Irish (5-0) on the cusp of making history again.
